title: What you see when a pack is opened
summary: Opening a pack in TCG Card Shop Simulator is a sequence of its own: the game spawns the cards as objects, fans them out, shows how many there are and dresses the whole thing in its own screens.
body: A pack opening is a sequence. The game runs an opening sequence with its own interface rather than quietly adding cards to your collection, which is why unpacking has a shape to it.

The cards are real objects for a moment. Cards are spawned as three-dimensional objects that exist in the scene while a pack is open, which is why a reveal can be looked at from an angle instead of being a picture.
They are arranged rather than stacked. The game keeps a list of those objects, groups them and shuffles them into a fan, so the cards spread out instead of tumbling.
You are told how many there are. The sequence has a group for the count, so the number of cards is shown rather than counted by eye.
Cards have display settings of their own. The game keeps settings for how a card is displayed, which is why the reveal obeys rules rather than being one fixed animation.
A card can be priced straight from it. There is a price popup of its own, so a card that is worth something can be dealt with at the moment you see it.
What this entry does not tell you: the odds inside a pack, how many cards one holds, or how long the sequence runs. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Opening a pack runs as a sequence with its own interface.
Cards are spawned as objects in the scene while the pack is open.
The open cards are listed, grouped and shuffled into a fan.
The sequence shows how many cards there are.
Cards have display settings of their own.
A card can be priced from the reveal.
